{{Expand German|topic=bio|Herman Auerbach|date=December 2009}}

'''Herman Auerbach''' (October 26, 1901, [[Tarnopol]] – August 17, 1942) was a Polish [[mathematician]] and member of the [[Lwów School of Mathematics]].

Auerbach was professor at [[Lwów University]]. He is known for introducing the [[Auerbach's lemma]], a theorem in [[functional analysis]]. During the [[Second World War]], because of his [[Jewish]] descent, he was imprisoned by the [[Germany|Germans]] in the [[Lwów Ghetto]]. In 1942, he was murdered at [[Bełżec extermination camp]].<ref>{{cite journal |year=1945 |title=Notes |journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.]] |volume=51 |issue=11 |pages=868–873 |doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1945-08465-1 |doi-access=free }} News on wartime fates of Polish mathematicians, pp. 868–869.</ref>
